notes: firstLevelDatPath (line 1333-1346) runs `unzip -Z -1` (bare member listing, one path per line), strips __MACOSX/-prefixed entries (AppleDouble metadata macOS's Archive Utility and, historically, macOS's own zip tool inject) and blank lines, then takes `paths.first(where: { $0 == "level.dat" || $0.hasSuffix("/level.dat") })` -- the FIRST match in the zip's own internal member order, not the shortest path or an alphabetical sort. If a zip happened to list world_nether/level.dat before world/level.dat, MSC 1 would silently pick the nether dimension's level.dat instead -- this fixture pins that the selection is positional, not semantic, since a well-formed WorldSlotManager-produced archive (createSlot, line 391) always writes the main world folder first and this ordering assumption has gone unnoticed as a result.
